findings.claim: P1: Element-local, stateless mouse listeners lose releases outside the terminal and synthesize drag reports for presses that began elsewhere.
findings.evidence: InputHandler registers mousedown/move/up only on the terminal element and treats any move with event.buttons != 0 as a drag. A forced press on the element followed by document mouseup emitted only ESC[<0;2;2M; a forced mousemove entering the element with buttons=1 emitted orphan ESC[<32;2;2M.
findings.layer: browser event topology and end-to-end PTY byte stream
findings.path: InputHandler element listeners -> handleMouse -> WTerm onData

findings.claim: P1: The new mouse/focus capability does not cross the advertised pluggable TerminalCore boundary, so Ghostty-backed WTerm instances silently disable it.
findings.evidence: The new TerminalCore accessors are optional and InputHandler defaults their absence to disabled. GhosttyCore implements none of mouseTracking/mouseSgr/focusEvents, its Zig export layer exposes only cursor_keys_app, bracketed_paste, and using_alt_screen, and the committed ghostty-vt.wasm has no mouse/focus exports. Therefore applications can enable 1000/1002/1004/1006 in Ghostty while @wterm/dom emits nothing.
findings.path: TerminalCore -> GhosttyCore via inferred cochange; InputHandler optional chaining -> silent disabled state

findings.claim: P1: Mouse coordinates are calculated against the full .term-grid, including rendered scrollback, rather than the visible active terminal viewport.
findings.evidence: Renderer inserts .term-scrollback-row nodes into .term-grid before active rows, while handleMouse scales clientY across .term-grid.getBoundingClientRect() and clamps into bridge.getRows(). In a forced 80x40 active grid with an 800px grid rect, a click at y=410 emitted row 21 even though that point can be scrollback/first-visible-active content depending on scroll position; the mapping never subtracts scrollback rows or scrollTop.
findings.layer: rendered DOM geometry to terminal active-grid coordinates

findings.claim: P2: User-facing docs are missing for the new public methods/behavior, and the core README now falsely implies mouse tracking requires Ghostty.
findings.evidence: No README or docs page is in the diff. packages/@wterm/core/README.md:24 says to use @wterm/ghostty for mouse tracking, while the committed built-in WASM now exports and honors 1000/1002/1006; the WasmBridge method table ends at usingAltScreen and omits mouseTracking, mouseSgr, and focusEvents; @wterm/dom/docs likewise omit automatic mouse/focus PTY reports.
findings.path: packages/@wterm/core/src and packages/@wterm/dom/src -> package READMEs and docs app

findings.claim: The built-in core silently ignores xterm mode 1003 any-motion tracking.
findings.evidence: Forcing ESC[?1003h followed by ESC[?1006h through the committed WASM produced getMouseTracking() == 0 and getMouseSgr() == 1; the parser, TerminalCore union, and DOM move guard enumerate only 1000 and 1002.
findings.path: Zig private-mode parser -> WASM accessor -> TerminalCore union -> DOM move guard
